text:
marta-cs: Customer (BrightArc) escalated — they upgraded mid-cycle from Starter -> Dedicated yesterday but were charged full Dedicated price on invoice INV-2026-701 instead of prorated. Customer has a PO (PO-9981) and needs a credit note + partial refund for the overlap. They also flagged VAT line looks doubled. Can finance advise how to proceed?

lee-billing: sorry seeing this now. Can you paste invoice JSON or screenshot? Need invoice id, invoice date, and the subscription change event id. Also: was the upgrade processed as immediate or scheduled?

marta-cs: pasted snippet from billing UI: ``invoice_id: INV-2026-701, created_at: 2026-02-18T14:03:22Z, amount_due: 120000, currency: USD, tax: 20000, metadata: {customer_id: CUST-470, po: PO-9981}`` Upgrade event: SUB_EVT_98765 (applied 2026-02-17T07:12:10Z) They expected proration credit for unused Starter days.

kai-support: quick repro: in staging run `GET /v1/billing/invoices/INV-2026-701` returns line_items: [ {plan: "starter", period: "2026-02-01 -> 2026-03-01", amount: 50000}, {plan: "dedicated", period: "2026-02-17 -> 2026-03-01", amount: 120000} ] total calculation didn't subtract prorated starter credit. Looks like proration engine double-counted tax on both lines.

billing-bot: invoice INV-2026-701 created for CUST-470 (PO-9981) — amount_due: 120000 USD — status: open. Reference: internal-task-1224.

sarah-finance: thanks. Two pieces: 1) customer-facing fix (credit note + partial refund or offset on next invoice) 2) ledger treatment and GL codes for manual credit. Do we have approval flow for >$1k adjustments? Need manager sign-off.

marta-cs: customer asking for immediate partial refund to their card on file if possible, otherwise a credit note they can apply to future invoices. Card attempted last week and failed (card decline code: card_declined, decline_reason: insufficient_funds). They re-submitted a new payment method today.

lee-billing: given PO requirement we should issue a credit note (CN) tied to the original invoice and mark it as 'applied' to INV-2026-701 if they request offset, or do an external refund once payments clear. Propose creating manual credit note that offsets prorated amount + VAT. I will draft numbers.

kai-support: quick calc I ran (rough): Starter monthly: $50.00 (50000 cents), Dedicated monthly: $120.00 (120000 cents). Upgrade on 2026-02-17 => 14 days of Starter used (Feb 1–17) and 14 days remaining. Prorated starter credit = (120000 - 50000) * (remaining_days / total_days)? Wait that's wrong — correct approach: credit unused starter days: 50000 * (remaining_days / 28) = 50000 * 14/28 = 25000. Charge for dedicated for remaining days = 120000 * 14/28 = 60000. Net delta = 60000 - 25000 = 35000. But invoice shows full 120000 — so missing applying -25000 starter credit. Tax calculation should be on net delta often, not both lines separately. Tax overcharged by ~?? (example: tax rate 10% => tax on both lines = (50000+120000)*0.1=17000 vs tax on net=35000*0.1=3500 difference 13500).

lee-billing: good calc. Let's compute with real VAT value from invoice: tax: 20000 cents. That matches if system taxed both lines separately. So adjustment = -25000 (credit) and -? tax adjustment = -? We'll compute precise tax to issue CN.

sarah-finance: need final numbers for CN description and GL mapping. Use GL account 4102 (Sales invoices) negative entry and 2200 (VAT payable) for tax reversal. Also require manager approval snippet: "approve_adj_#1224" from finance manager.

marta-cs: customer confirmed they'd accept credit note applied to invoice if we can do that today. They also sent approved PO copy (attached in thread) and asked to ensure CN references PO-9981.

lee-billing: drafting CN now. Proposed CN line items: - Prorated starter credit: -25000 cents (USD) - VAT reversal: -2500 cents (assuming 10% tax applied on credit) Total CN amount: -27500 cents. Reference: CN-2026-045. Posting: credit invoice INV-2026-701, mark applied. If customer later wants cash refund we'll process after payment method validates.

nina-legal: flag — make sure CN language includes "Non-deductible fees"? (no) — actually ensure CN states reason: "proration credit due to mid-cycle plan upgrade" and include PO number. Also confirm tax country rules: if invoice VAT was reported, reversing VAT requires us to issue CN with VAT lines matching original rates.

lee-billing: yes will include PO-9981 and exact VAT rate 8% per customer's billing address (weird, invoice had 20000 cents which corresponds to ~11.8% on 170000 base — need to reconcile). I'll pull original tax rate from customer record.

kai-support: small repro note for eng: suspected bug in proration pipeline when upgrade_subscribe_immediate flag is true + PO present. Repro steps: 1) create customer with PO metadata 2) create starter subscription 3) create immediate upgrade to dedicated using upgrade_subscribe_immediate=true 4) generate invoice for current period 5) observe line_items shows both full plan lines w/o negative prorate credit. I've attached request to eng-runtime.

billing-bot: ticket created: TICK-4721 "proration missing when upgrade immediate + PO metadata" — assigned to eng-runtime.

sarah-finance: manager approval: @simon-finance please approve manual CN-2026-045 for -27500 cents GL 4102/2200.

simon-finance (reaction): :thumbsup:

simon-finance: approved. please proceed and attach CN PDF and journal entry to the internal ticket.

lee-billing: done — created CN-2026-045, applied to INV-2026-701. Journal entry JE-8892 created. Files uploaded to internal drive. I'll hold refund until payment method validated per finance rules.

marta-cs: relayed to customer: "we've applied a credit note (CN-2026-045) for $275.00 to your invoice INV-2026-701; if you'd prefer a refund we can issue after payment method validation." Customer replied :thumbsup:.

kai-support: marking thread resolved for now. Eng assigned. Will follow up if we see further repros.

lee-billing: note for audit: CN reason: "proration credit for mid-cycle upgrade (failed application of proration engine)" — link to TICK-4721 and JE-8892.

marta-cs: thanks all — closing on customer side.
